correctness.rationale: Every face of the Alexander dual has size at most five: below size four vacuous; size four induced P4/claw; size five exactly C5; size six impossible by incompatible degree-two constraints on each deleted five-cycle. A P4 belongs to at most one C5, and its single-edge-plus-isolated triangle is in at most the two neighboring P4 tetrahedra of that pentagon; a claw has a unique independent-leaf triangle. Collapsing each C5 four-simplex with one private tetrahedron and then collapsing remaining P4 and claw tetrahedra along demonstrably free triangles eliminates all cells above dimension two. The original dual was simply connected as it has full two-skeleton, so the residue is a wedge of B(G) 2-spheres. Exact simplex Euler counting gives B=binom(n-1,3)-c4+p5 and c4 equals the degree formula. Integral Alexander duality gives original homology only in degree n-5; original cut complex contains full (n-7)-skeleton and is simply connected for n>=9. Inductive Hurewicz and Whitehead give the integral wedge homotopy type. The standard-library sample checker independently tests face counts, mod-two ranks and legal collapses; finite checks do not replace this uniform proof. No assertion for n<=8.

originality.rationale: The already established girth-five Euler formula (Bayer et al. 2024, Proposition 2.18) is expressly not claimed novel. The new stronger theorem proves a complete integral homotopy classification for every graph of girth at least five and n >= 9, by a dual free-face collapse tolerating pentagons with shared graph edges. Inspected nearest general wedge result assumes girth >= 6 at cut size four, and the four-cycle correction theorem treats cut size three. Exact older Petersen/cycle/forest cases are subsumed as acknowledged prior special cases. Residual possibility: uncatalogued equivalent homotopy classification.

value.rationale: The girth-five threshold is a mathematically natural boundary: it introduces pentagonal four-simplices in the Alexander dual and invalidates the simpler girth-six private-face argument. Proposition 2.18 of the primary sequel already provides Euler correction but not the homotopy type. The new uniform free-face mechanism deals with overlapping pentagons without requiring edge disjointness, upgrades a numerical invariant to a complete integral homotopy theorem for arbitrary graphs of girth >=5, and provides an explicit dodecahedral instance. This is a motivated structural theorem, not a routine numerical increment or a mere recomputation of the Euler characteristic.
